A physical game — no screens required

Brain training

What is Mindathon?

A physical game that turns brain training into play

Mindathon is a physical cognitive training game. Players take part in challenges that call on their memory, focus, speed and problem-solving — responding with their hands, voice and full attention.

Instead of watching or tapping a screen, players are actively thinking, responding and participating. That makes brain training feel like a game, not a chore.

  • Hands-on challenges — you take part, you don't just watch.
  • Made for groups — play with family, classmates or friends.
  • Designed by a memory trainer with 33 years of experience.
Why Brain Training?

Skills that benefit from practice

Just as physical activity exercises the body, regular mental challenges give cognitive skills opportunities to be practised and developed.

Practise, not just watch

Active responding builds engagement in a way passive watching cannot match.

Structured challenge

Clear challenges at rising difficulty give learners a steady, meaningful path.

Fun keeps people coming back

When training feels like a game, people willingly practise again and again.

Six Cognitive Areas

What Mindathon is designed to practise

Every challenge in Mindathon supports one or more of these cognitive areas.

01

Memory & Recall

Challenges that practise holding, storing and retrieving information.

02

Focus & Attention

Challenges that require attention, concentration and ignoring distractions.

03

Problem Solving

Challenges that ask players to reason, plan and work things out.

04

Mental Speed & Accuracy

Challenges that practise quick, precise thinking and responding.

05

Mental Flexibility

Challenges that practise switching between rules, tasks and ideas.

06

Confidence & Positive Attitude

Challenges that encourage players to try, respond and stay positive.

Meet Mindathon

A game you can hold in your hands

No apps to install, no accounts to create. Mindathon is a physical game that gets people thinking, responding and participating together.

Active, not passive

You respond, you participate. That's the difference from watching a video.

Built for variety

Different challenges call on different cognitive skills — memory one moment, speed the next.

Meant to be shared

Designed for family time, classrooms, centres and group activities.

How It Works

The Mindathon experience in four steps

01

Choose a challenge

Pick from a range of cognitive challenges with different demands.

02

Think

Look, listen and understand what the challenge is asking.

03

Play & respond

Respond actively — with speed, accuracy and full attention.

04

Practise & improve

Play again, take on harder challenges and watch your progress.
